**Finding: missing (high severity) — Termination for convenience**

- **What the document says:** Section 11.1 binds us to a five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals; Section 11.2 allows termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. A full-text search confirmed the only other exits are the acceptance-test failure right (§3) and warranty/IP remedies (§§7–8) — none is a convenience right.
- **Direction check:** Commerce One (Vendor) has no convenience right either, so nothing needs deleting on that side; the gap is entirely on our side as Licensee/Customer.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** New Section 11.4 inserted after §11.3 (avoids renumbering) giving Corio a 30-day convenience termination, in whole or in part, without penalty or early-termination fee, with refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period, and expressly confirming Commerce One has no convenience exit during the initial or renewal terms.
- **Fallback offered in the comment:** 60–90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
